Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:11:1.hebrew: ש"מ מדר' אמי - דשני הא מילתא — תלתא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:11:1.english: Conclude from it from Rabbi Ami - Who resolved this matter — [namely,] three [rulings]:

Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:11:2.hebrew: ושמע מינה פרוטה ומלוה דעתה אפרוטה - מדשנייה למתני' הכי, דכי יש באחרונה ש"פ מקודשת, ואע"ג דקמייתא מלוה הויא בהדה ובכולהו קדשה — דהא כללא חשיב ליה גבי מנחת, וקאמר דאם יש בכולן שוה פרוטה מקודשת, אלמא קידושי אכולהו קיימי — אפ"ה גבי אוכלת, דהוו להו מלוה ופרוטה, מקודשת באחרונה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:11:2.english: And conclude from it: [In the case of] a peruta and a loan, her mind is on the peruta - [This is deduced] from the fact that [Rabbi Ami] resolved the Mishnah in this way: that when the last [date] has the value of a peruta, she is betrothed; and even though the earlier [dates] were a loan in her possession and he had betrothed her with all of them — for [the Mishnah] considers it a collective [betrothal] in the case of [a woman who] sets them down, and states that if all of them together are worth a peruta she is betrothed, which shows that the betrothal rests upon all of them — even so, in the case of [a woman who] eats [them], where they have become a loan and a peruta, she is betrothed by the last [date].

Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:11:3.hebrew: ש"מ המקדש במלוה אינה מקודשת - מדקביל הך אתקפתא דפרכינן לעיל: "והא מלוה היא", ואיזדקיק לשנויי עלה: "מאי באחת? באחרונה קאמר" — אלמא ס"ל שאינה מקודשת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:11:3.english: Conclude from it: One who betroths [a woman] with a loan, she is not betrothed - Since [Rabbi Ami] accepted this objection that we raised above: "But it is a loan!", and saw fit to answer regarding it: "What is [meant by] 'with one'? He meant: With the last one" — evidently he holds that she is not betrothed.

Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:11:4.hebrew: ושמע מינה פרוטה ומלוה דעתה אפרוטה - מדשנייה למתני' הכי, דכי יש באחרונה ש"פ מקודשת, ואע"ג דקמייתא מלוה הויא בהדה ובכולהו קדשה — דהא כללא חשיב ליה גבי מנחת, וקאמר דאם יש בכולן שוה פרוטה מקודשת, אלמא קידושי אכולהו קיימי — אפ"ה גבי אוכלת, דהוו להו מלוה ופרוטה, מקודשת באחרונה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:11:4.english: And conclude from it: [In the case of] a peruta and a loan, her mind is on the peruta - [This is deduced] from the fact that [Rabbi Ami] resolved the Mishnah in this way: that when the last [date] has the value of a peruta, she is betrothed; and even though the earlier [dates] were a loan in her possession and he had betrothed her with all of them — for [the Mishnah] considers it a collective [betrothal] in the case of [a woman who] sets them down, and states that if all of them together are worth a peruta she is betrothed, which shows that the betrothal rests upon all of them — even so, in the case of [a woman who] eats [them], where they have become a loan and a peruta, she is betrothed by the last [date].

Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:1:1.hebrew: נראין דברי תלמיד - עולא קמסיים למילתיה ואזיל, וקאמר: נראין דברי ר' ירמיה, שהוא תלמידו של רב הונא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:1:1.english: The statement of the student seems reasonable - Ulla is going on to conclude his statement, and saying: The statement of Rav Yirmeya seems reasonable, as he is the student of Rav Huna.

Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:1:2.hebrew: הואיל ונעשה בה מעשה יתומה בחיי האב - בחייו קידשה והשיאה עצמה שלא לדעתו, כאילו היא יתומה, והוא ראה ושתק: או הפקיר זכות שיש לו בה, או שתיקתו הודאה. דבשלמא נתקדשה לדעתו וניסת שלא לדעתו, איכא למימר: בחדא שתיקה מרתח רתח, אבל כולי האי לא שתיק:
Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:1:2.english: Since an action of an orphan was done with her in the lifetime of the father - During his lifetime she betrothed and married herself off without his consent, as if she were an orphan, and he saw and remained silent: either he renounced the right he has to her, or his silence is an admission of consent. For it is understandable if she was betrothed with his consent and married without his consent, one can say that with a single silence he was angry, but for all of this he would not remain silent.

Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:2:1.hebrew: יכולין לעכב - הואיל ובשעת קבלה לא נתרצה האב, אם באתה לחזור קודם שיתרצה האב, חוזרת, ולא מהניא תו ריצוי האב:
Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:2:1.english: Are able to prevent [the betrothal] - Since at the time of acceptance the father had not consented, if she comes to retract before the father consents, she may retract, and the father's consent is no longer effective.

Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:2:2.english: I have [no one] - who is able to refuse, except her father.

Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:2:3.hebrew: היא כו' - וקס"ד, בפיתה לשם קידושין אשמועינן קרא, ולמימר דמצי הדרה בה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:2:3.english: She, etc. - And it enters your mind [that] the verse teaches us [regarding a case where] he seduced her for the sake of betrothal, and to say that she can retract [her consent].

Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:3:1.english: Do not go after the opposite - [That is,] something that is not [so].

Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:3:2.english: He can answer you - The verse speaks of seduction not for the sake of betrothal.

Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:3:3.hebrew: קרא בעי - למימר דאביה יכול לעכב, וכן היא? ומהיכא תיתי לן לאוסרה בההיא בעילה, למימר קידושין הן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:3:3.english: Is a verse required - To say that her father can withhold consent, and likewise she? And from where would it occur to us to forbid her [to others] through that act of intercourse, to say that it is betrothal?

Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:3:4.hebrew: אמר ר"נ לומר שמשלם קנס כמפותה - קרא לאו לאשמועינן היתרא איצטריך, אלא לאשמועינן דכי מעכבא איהי נמי, משלם קנס כדין מפותה — שתלה הכתוב קנסא במיאון האב, הכי נמי תלי במיאון דידה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:3:4.english: Rav Naḥman said: To say that he pays a fine like a seduced woman - The verse was not needed to teach us permission [to refuse], but rather to teach us that when she withholds consent as well, he pays the fine in accordance with the law of a seduced woman — for [just as] Scripture conditioned the fine on the refusal of the father, so too it is conditioned on her refusal.

Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:4:1.english: If so - It is a support.

Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:4:2.english: This is - [It is] certainly that which we learned: “He shall pay a dowry for her...” etc.

Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:4:3.hebrew: אמר ליה - מהא לא תסייען, דאיכא למימר דמצריך לה בקידושי אחריני לדעת אביה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:4:3.english: [Abaye] said to him - Do not bring us support from this, for it can be said that [the baraita] requires her [to have] another betrothal with her father’s consent.

Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:5:1.hebrew: ואם לאו אינה מקודשת - דכיון דאמר ״התקדשי״, ״התקדשי״ — כל חדא וחדא הוו קידושין באנפי נפשייהו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:5:1.english: And if not, she is not betrothed - For since he said, “Be betrothed,” “Be betrothed,” each and every one was a betrothal in its own right.

Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:5:2.hebrew: ואם לאו אינה מקודשת - דכיון דאמר ״התקדשי״, ״התקדשי״, כל חדא וחדא הוו קידושין באנפי נפשייהו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:5:2.english: And if not, she is not betrothed - For since he said, “Be betrothed,” “Be betrothed,” each and every one was a betrothal in its own right.

Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:5:3.hebrew: היתה אוכלת ראשונה ראשונה - בגמרא מפרש לה אהייא קאי, וטעמא מאי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:5:3.english: [If] she was eating [them] one by one - In the Gemara, [it] explains to which [clause] it refers, and what the reason is.

Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:6:1.hebrew: מאן תנא התקדשי התקדשי - הוא דהוי פרטא, אבל בזו ובזו לאו פרטא הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:6:1.english: Who is the Tanna [who taught]: “Be betrothed,” “Be betrothed” - [That this] is what constitutes an individual specification, but [saying] “with this and with this” is not an individual specification.

Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:6:2.hebrew: אמר רבה ר"ש היא - בשבועות (דף לו:), גבי חמשה תובעין אותו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:6:2.english: Rabba said: It is Rabbi Shimon - In Shevuot (36b), regarding five [people who] claim from him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:7:1.english: To which - Does [the clause] “she was eating” refer?

Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:7:2.english: If we say [it refers] to the first clause - Where he said, "Be betrothed [to me], be betrothed [to me]."

Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:7:3.hebrew: אלא אסיפא - דחשיבא ליה כללא, קאמר דאם היתה אוכלת ראשונה ראשונה כו', וכי איכא בחדא שוה פרוטה — מיהא מיקדשא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:7:3.english: Rather, to the latter clause - Where it is considered by him a collective [statement], [the Mishnah] states that if she was eating them one by one, etc., and when there is the value of a peruta in one [of them], she is at least betrothed.

Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:8:1.hebrew: ואפילו בקמייתא - ואפילו הראשונה או השניה שוה פרוטה, אע"פ שאין באחרונה שוה פרוטה, מקודשת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:8:1.english: And even with the first - And even [if] the first or the second is worth a peruta, even though the last is not worth a peruta, she is betrothed.

Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:8:2.hebrew: והא מלוה היא - כיון דקידושין לא נגמרו עד שתקבלם כולם, והיא כבר אכלה את הראשונה קודם שתקנה אותה בקידושיה, הויא זו הראשונה מלוה גבה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:8:2.english: But it is a loan - Since the betrothal is not finalized until she receives all of them, and she already ate the first [date] before she acquired it through her betrothal, this first [date] becomes a loan owed by her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:8:3.hebrew: הרי שלחן כו' - כלומר, הרי לנו משנה שנויה, ואין אנו יודעים לפרשה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:8:3.english: There is a table, etc. - That is to say, behold, we have a taught Mishnah, yet we do not know how to explain it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:9:1.hebrew: ומיקרבא הנייתה - מוכנת היתה הנייתה, וגלתה את לבה שהיתה חפיצה בהן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 46a:9:1.english: And her benefit is close [at hand] - Her benefit was readily available, and she revealed her heart, that she desired them.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 46a:1:1.hebrew: נראין דברי תלמיד - משמע הכא דרב ירמיה תלמידיה דרב הונא הוה. וקשה, דבפרק תפלת השחר (ברכות דף כז:) משמע דתלמיד חבר דרב הוה, דקאמר התם: רב צלי של שבת בע"ש, א"ל רב ירמיה בר אבא: "מי בדלת?", א"ל: "אין, בדילנא". ומדלא קאמר ליה רב ירמיה: "מי בדיל מר?", שמע מינה שהיה לו תלמיד חבר. ונראה דתרי רב ירמיה הוו:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 46a:1:1.english: "The statement of the student seems [reasonable]" - This implies here that Rav Yirmeya was a disciple of Rav Huna. And this is difficult, as in the chapter [entitled] Tefillat HaShachar (Berakhot 27b), it implies that he was a disciple-colleague of Rav, for it says there: Rav prayed [the prayer] of Shabbat on the eve of Shabbat. Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said to him, "Have you ceased [from labor]?" He said to him, "Yes, I have ceased." And since Rav Yirmeya did not say to him, "Has the Master ceased?", conclude from this that he was a disciple-colleague to him. And it appears that there were two [sages named] Rav Yirmeya.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 46a:2:1.hebrew: אמר רב יוסף אי הכי - בניחותא, וסייעתא היא. וכן היה רב יוסף רגיל לומר, כדאמרינן בפרק במה מדליקין (שבת דף כח.): "א"ה היינו דמתרגמינן ססגונא". א"ל אביי: "צריכה קידושין כו'" — ולא תסייעיה מהא. וי"מ דר"נ בא ליישב: "לעולם אימא לך שפיתה לשם אישות", וגרסי' "אלא אמר ר"נ". ולא תימא דתיקשי לרב אסי דאמר "אביה ולא היא" — דהא דקאמר הכא דיכולה למאן, אינו ר"ל דלא תהא אשתו, כיון דרוצה אביה אינה יכולה לעכב; אלא ר"ל שמשלם קנס כמפותה, כלומר: כדין שאר מפותות שהאב ממאן, כדפי' בקונטרס. ופריך רב יוסף בתמיה: "אי הכי כו'":
Tosafot on Kiddushin 46a:2:1.english: Rav Yosef said: If so - [This statement was spoken] in a declarative tone, and it is a support [for Rav's explanation]. And so Rav Yosef was accustomed to say, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Madlikin (Shabbat 28a): "If so, that is what we translate [as] sasgona." Abaye said to him: "She requires betrothal, etc." — [meaning,] do not support him from this. And some explain that Rav Naḥman came to resolve [the objection against Rav Asi]: "Actually, I could say to you that he seduced her for the sake of marriage," and the textual reading is: "Rather, Rav Naḥman said." And do not say that this poses a difficulty for Rav Asi, who said: "Her father [can prevent], but not she," for that which [the baraita] says here that she is able to refuse does not mean that she will not be his wife — since her father desires [the marriage], she cannot prevent [it] — but rather, it means that he pays a fine like a seduced maiden, that is, in accordance with the law of other seduced maidens whose father refuses, as explained in the Kuntres. And Rav Yosef objected in astonishment: "If so, etc."

Tosafot on Kiddushin 46a:2:2.hebrew: בין היא בין אביה יכולין לעכב - ואע"ג דאמר רב לעיל (קידושין דף מד:): חיישינן שמא נתרצה האב — היינו בסתמא, ששמע ושתק; אבל היכא דמיחה, גילה בדעתו. ולא מיבעיא אם לא נתרצה האב שיכולה היא לעכב, אלא אפי' נתרצה האב יכולה לעכב. וא"ת: מה יועיל שתעכב אחרי שיתרצה האב, הא בידו לקדשה בעל כרחה? וי"ל: היינו דוקא בתחילת הקידוש; אבל היכא דנתקדשה שלא לדעת אביה, ואח"כ נתרצה האב, ואתה רוצה לומר דמקודשת מטעם דזכות הוא לו — אמרינן: כיון דבתו מעכבת, דחוב הוא לו, ולא היה מתרצה אם היה יודע דמעכבה. ומיהו לפירוש הקונטרס לא קשיא מידי, דפי': הואיל ובשעת קבלת הקידושין לא נתרצה האב, אם באתה לחזור קודם שיתרצה האב — חוזרת, ולא מהני תו רצוי האב:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 46a:2:2.english: "Either she or her father is able to prevent" - And even though Rav said above (Kiddushin 44b) that we are concerned lest the father consented, that is in an unspecified case, where he heard and was silent; but where he protested, he revealed his intention. And it is not only necessary [to state that] if the father did not consent, she can prevent [it]; rather, even if the father consented, she can prevent [it]. And if you say: What will it avail that she prevents [it] after the father consents, given that it is in his power to betroth her against her will? And one can say: That is specifically at the beginning of the betrothal; but where she was betrothed without her father's knowledge, and afterwards the father consented, and you wish to say that she is betrothed on the grounds that it is an advantage to him — we say: since his daughter objects, it is a disadvantage to him, and he would not have consented had he known that she objects. However, according to Rashi's explanation, this poses no difficulty at all, for he explained: Since at the time of the receipt of the betrothal [money] the father had not consented, if she came to retract before the father consented, she may retract, and the father's consent is no longer effective.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 46a:3:1.hebrew: קרא בעיא - פי': שלא תהא אשתו באותה ביאה — פשיטא, דהא אפילו לא ימאנו אינה אשתו בהך ביאה, כיון שפיתה שלא לשם אישות. בשלמא אם פיתה לשם אישות — אשמועינן חידוש, דבין היא ובין אביה יכולין לעכב; אבל השתא, מאי חידוש אשמועינן? וליכא למימר דקרא ה"ק: שאם יבא אביה לקדשה לאותו מפתה שתוכל בתו למאן — דפשיטא שיכול לקדשה בע"כ! ומשני: "לומר שמשלם קנס כמפותה". פי': לעולם מיירי שפיתה שלא לשם אישות, ואפ"ה אשמועינן רבותא דכי מעכבא איהי שמשלם קנס; דכמו דתלה הכתוב קנס דמפותה במיאון האב, כך תלאו במיאון דידה. והאי מיאון דידה ודאי אינו מועיל לענין שלא תינשא לו, דכיון דאביה רוצה שתהא אשתו אינה יכולה לעכב, אלא מהני שמשלם קנס כאילו האב ממאן. א"נ, נפקא מינה היכא דבא עליה ואח"כ נתייתמה, דהשתא מהני מיאון דידה לעכב שלא תהא אשתו:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 46a:3:1.english: Is a verse required? - Explanation: That she should not become his wife through that act of intercourse is obvious, for even if they do not refuse, she is not his wife through this act of intercourse, since he seduced her not for the sake of marriage. It is well if he seduced her for the sake of marriage: [the verse] would teach us a novel ruling, that both she and her father can prevent [the marriage]. But now, what novelty does [the verse] teach us? And one cannot say that the verse means as follows: that if her father comes to betroth her to that seducer, his daughter can refuse — for it is obvious that [the father] can betroth her against her will! And [the Gemara] answers: "To say that he pays a fine like a seduced woman." Explanation: Actually, [the baraita] is dealing with [a case where] he seduced her not for the sake of marriage, and even so, it teaches us a novel point: that when she objects, he pays a fine; for just as Scripture made the fine of a seduced woman dependent on the refusal of the father, so too it made it dependent on her refusal. And this refusal of hers certainly is not effective to prevent her from marrying him, for since her father wants her to be his wife, she cannot prevent [it]; rather, [her refusal] is effective [in] that he pays a fine, as if the father refused. Alternatively, a practical difference [where her refusal does prevent the marriage] is where he had intercourse with her and afterwards she became orphaned, so that now her refusal is effective to prevent her from becoming his wife.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 46a:4:1.hebrew: אמר רב יוסף אי הכי - בניחותא, וסייעתא היא. וכן היה רב יוסף רגיל לומר, כדאמרינן בפרק במה מדליקין (שבת דף כח.): "א"ה, היינו דמתרגמינן ססגונא". א"ל אביי: "צריכה קידושין" כו' — ולא תסייעיה מהא. וי"מ דר"נ בא ליישב: "לעולם אימא לך שפיתה לשם אישות", וגרסי': "אלא אמר ר"נ". ולא תימא דתיקשי לרב אסי, דאמר: "אביה ולא היא" — דהא דקאמר הכא דיכולה למאן, אינו ר"ל דלא תהא אשתו, כיון דרוצה אביה אינה יכולה לעכב; אלא ר"ל שמשלם קנס כמפותה, כלומר כדין שאר מפותות שהאב ממאן, כדפי' בקונטרס. ופריך רב יוסף בתמיה: "אי הכי" כו':
Tosafot on Kiddushin 46a:4:1.english: Rav Yosef said: "If so" - [This was stated] in an affirmative tone, and it is a support [for the preceding view]. And Rav Yosef was accustomed to say this, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Madlikin (Shabbat 28a): "If so, that is why we translate [it as] sasgona." Abaye said to him: "She requires betrothal..." etc. — [meaning:] and do not support him from this. And some explain that Rav Naḥman came to resolve [the difficulty by saying]: "Actually, I can tell you that he seduced her for the sake of marriage," and we read [the text as]: "Rather, Rav Naḥman said." And do not say that this poses a difficulty to Rav Asi, who said: "Her father, but not she" — for that which [the baraita] says here that she can refuse does not mean that she will not become his wife, for since her father desires [the marriage], she cannot prevent [it]; rather, it means that he pays a fine like a seduced woman, that is, according to the law of other seduced women whose father refuses [to give her in marriage], as explained in the Kuntres. And Rav Yosef objects in astonishment: "If so..." etc.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 46a:8:1.hebrew: ואפילו בקמייתא - פי' בקונטרס: אפילו הראשונה או השניה שוה פרוטה, אע"ג דאין באחרונה שוה פרוטה — מקודשת? "והא מלוה היא" — כיון דהקידושין לא נגמרו עד שתקבלם כולם, והיא אכלה הראשונה כבר קודם שתקנה אותה בקידושין, הויין מלוה גבה. וא"ת: כיון דבתורת קידושין אתו לידה, היכי הוה מלוה? הא אמרינן לקמן בפרק האומר (קידושין דף נט.): האומר לאשה "התקדשי לי לאחר ל' יום", אפי' נתאכלו המעות — מקודשת! אלמא לאו מלוה נינהו היכא דבתורת קידושין אתו לידה. וי"ל: דיש לחלק, דהתם הרי הדיבור נגמר קודם שנתאכלו; אבל הכא, דלא נגמרו הקידושין עד אחר מסירה אחרונה, ובתוך כך אכלה הראשונה והשניה — איכא למימר דמלוה הן אצלה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 46a:8:1.english: "And even with the first one?" - Rashi explained in the Kunteres: [Does the Mishnah mean that] even if [only] the first or the second is worth a peruta, even though there is not a peruta's worth in the last one, she is betrothed? "But it is a loan!" — since the betrothal is not completed until she receives all of them, and she already ate the first one before he acquired her in betrothal, they become a loan in her possession. And if you say: Since they came into her hand as betrothal [money], how does it become a loan? Behold, we say later in the chapter [entitled] HaOmer (Kiddushin 59a): [In the case of] one who says to a woman, "Be betrothed to me after thirty days," even if the money was consumed, she is betrothed! This shows that they are not [considered] a loan where they came into her hand as betrothal [money]. And one can say: A distinction can be made: For there, the declaration was concluded before they were consumed; but here, where the betrothal was not completed until after the final delivery, and in the meantime she ate the first and the second, it can be said that they are a loan in her possession.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 46a:9:1.hebrew: [אימא גמרה ומקניא כו' - אע"ג דלא תלו בדידה להתקדש בפחות משוה פרוטה, כדאמרינן בפ"ק — מיהו בקל עושה צריכותא] ת"י:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 46a:9:1.english: ["Say that she has decided to transfer herself, etc." - Even though it does not depend on her to become betrothed with less than the value of a peruta, as we say in the first chapter — nonetheless, [the Gemara] readily constructs a tzrikhta [to explain why both cases are needed].] — Tosafot Yeshanim.
